newsitem.title: HONG KONG: APP Global Finance raises FRN to US$600 mln.
newsitem.headline: APP Global Finance raises FRN to US$600 mln.

text.p: APP Global Finance has increased its five-year floating rate note issue to US$600 million from US$500 million owing to strong demand in syndication, bankers said Tuesday.
Proceeds of the issue will ultimately be used by Asia Pulp and Paper.
The notes were priced at par to float at 400 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate. With fees, the all-in return to top-tier participants is 435 basis points.

Nine banks joined Union Bank of Switzerland, Singapore branch, as arranger of the transaction. They are Chaio Tung Bank, Chung Sing Bank, Cosmo Bank Taiwan Offshore Banking Branch, Daewoo Securities, First Commercial Bank, Korea First Finance, Korea Merchant Banking Corp, Maybank International (L) Ltd and UMBC International Bank.

Lead managers are UBS Singapore branch, Bear Stearns Asia, Fuji International Finance (HK), IBJ Asia, Nippon Credit International (HK), Peregrine Fixed Income, Sumitomo Finance (Asia) and UMBC International Bank (L) Ltd.

Co-lead managers are Chiao Tung Bank, Chung Shing Bank, Cosmos Bank Taiwan Offshore Banking branch, First Commercial Bank, Korea Merchant Banking Corp, Daewoo Securities, SsangYong Investment and Securities Co.

Co-managers are AMMB International (L), Australian and New Zealand Banking Group, Bank of Commerce (L), DCB Bank (L), Maybank International (L), Pan Asia Bank, United World Chinese Commercial Bank, Yeungnam Merchant Banking Corp, PT Bank Ekspor Impor Indonesia Singapore branch, KMBC Asia Ltd, Bayerische Vereinsbank AG Singapore branch, Chungbu Leasing and Finance (HK), Coryo Merchant Bank, Development Bank of Singapore, Dong Ah Securities, Donghwa Bank, Gyongnam Merchant Banking Corp, Korea First Finance, Kwangju Bank, Nara Banking Corp, Nomura Singapore, Overseas Chinese Bank, PT Bank Bali acting through its Cayman Islands branch, Samsam Merchant Bank, ABN AMRO Bank Singapore branch, Credit Lyonnais, Daiwa Singapore, Far Eastern International Bank, Fubon Commercial Bank, HanGil Merchant Banking Corp, Hanwha Merchant Bank, Kangwon Bank, KDLC Leasing Singapore, KFB Securities Co, Lehman Brothers Securities Asia, LG Merchant Banking Corp, Oversea-Chinese Banking Corp, Overseas Union Bank, Salomon Brothers Hong Kong, Shinhan Investment Bank and Yamaichi Merchant Bank (Singapore).
The notes will be free to trade at 0930 Singapore time Wednesday, September 25. Prices will be quoted on the Bond Quotation System (BQS) operated by the Stock Exchange of Singapore.
Signing of the transaction is set for October 2 in Singapore. The payment and closing date is October 4.
